source: Biên soạn theo format TOEIC Listening & Reading — chỉ phần Reading (Part 5, 6, 7)

part5.question: The new marketing strategy was _______ successful in attracting younger customers.
part5.explain: Cần một trạng từ (adverb) để bổ nghĩa cho tính từ 'successful'. 'Highly' mang nghĩa là rất, cực kỳ.

part5.question: All employees must submit _______ expense reports by the end of the month.
part5.explain: Cần một tính từ sở hữu (possessive adjective) đứng trước danh từ 'expense reports'. 'Their' là lựa chọn đúng.

part5.question: The seminar on time management will begin _______ 9:00 AM tomorrow.
part5.explain: Dùng giới từ 'at' trước một giờ cụ thể (9:00 AM).

part5.question: Mr. Lee is _______ for training the new staff members next week.
part5.explain: Cấu trúc 'be responsible for' (chịu trách nhiệm cho việc gì). Cần tính từ ở đây.

part5.question: The factory will halt production _______ the machine undergoes maintenance.
part5.explain: 'while' + mệnh đề (the machine undergoes maintenance). 'during', 'because of', 'despite' cộng với danh từ/cụm danh từ.

part5.question: We apologize for any _______ this delay may cause.
part5.explain: Sau 'any' cần một danh từ không đếm được hoặc số nhiều. 'inconvenience' (sự bất tiện) phù hợp ngữ cảnh.

part5.question: The restaurant is offering a 20% discount _______ regular customers.
part5.explain: 'offer a discount to someone' (giảm giá cho ai).

part5.question: Ms. Garcia _______ the financial report before she left the office.
part5.explain: Hành động đã hoàn thành trong quá khứ trước khi rời đi (left the office). 'finished' là thì quá khứ đơn phù hợp.

part5.question: Please ensure that your password is kept _______ at all times.
part5.explain: Cấu trúc 'keep + object + adjective' (giữ cho cái gì đó như thế nào). Cần tính từ 'secure'.

part5.question: The board of directors approved the budget _______ the project.
part5.explain: 'budget for something' (ngân sách cho việc gì).

part5.question: _______ the bad weather, the outdoor company picnic has been postponed.
part5.explain: 'the bad weather' là cụm danh từ. Cần giới từ 'Due to'. 'Because' và 'Even though' cần mệnh đề.

part5.question: The CEO suggested _______ a new branch in Tokyo to expand the Asian market.
part5.explain: Động từ 'suggest' + V-ing. Nên 'opening' là đúng.

part5.question: Only applicants _______ meet the minimum requirements will be contacted for an interview.
part5.explain: Đại từ quan hệ thay thế cho 'applicants' (người) và đóng vai trò làm chủ ngữ cho động từ 'meet'. Dùng 'who'.

part5.question: The software update is expected to run _______ than the previous version.
part5.explain: Cần một trạng từ để bổ nghĩa cho động từ 'run', và dạng so sánh hơn vì có 'than'. 'more smoothly' là đúng.

part5.question: If we had known about the delay, we _______ our flight.
part5.explain: Câu điều kiện loại 3 diễn tả sự việc không có thật trong quá khứ: If + S + had + V3/ed, S + would have + V3/ed.

part5.question: The financial documents must be reviewed _______ by the auditors before submission.
part5.explain: Cần trạng từ bổ nghĩa cho động từ 'reviewed'. 'thoroughly' (một cách kỹ lưỡng) là đáp án đúng.

part5.question: _______ the presentation was long, the audience remained engaged throughout.
part5.explain: 'the presentation was long' là mệnh đề. Nghĩa tương phản nên dùng 'Although'. 'Despite' đi với cụm danh từ.

part5.question: By this time next year, the construction of the new headquarters _______.
part5.explain: Dấu hiệu 'By this time next year' chỉ tương lai hoàn thành. Việc xây dựng phải được hoàn thành (bị động).

part5.question: Neither the manager _______ the employees were aware of the policy change.
part5.explain: Cấu trúc tương quan 'Neither ... nor ...' (Không ... cũng không ...).

part5.question: The committee has reached a _______ regarding the upcoming merger.
part5.explain: Cần một danh từ sau 'a'. 'consensus' (sự đồng thuận) là từ vựng chính xác trong ngữ cảnh họp hành, hội đồng.

part5.question: Had the marketing team launched the campaign earlier, sales _______ significantly.
part5.explain: Đảo ngữ câu điều kiện loại 3: Had + S + V3/ed, S + would have + V3/ed.

part5.question: The newly appointed director is highly regarded for her _______ in corporate litigation.
part5.explain: Sau tính từ sở hữu 'her' cần danh từ. 'expertise' (sự chuyên môn, chuyên môn) là đúng.

part5.question: Any staff members _______ to volunteer for the charity event should notify human resources.
part5.explain: Rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ chủ động: 'who wish' -> 'wishing'.

part5.question: It is imperative that the safety protocols _______ strictly followed by all personnel.
part5.explain: Cấu trúc giả định cách với 'imperative': It is imperative that + S + (should) + V_bare. Nên động từ to be ở dạng nguyên thể là 'be'.

part5.question: The sales figures for this quarter are considerably lower _______ those of the same period last year.
part5.explain: Có so sánh hơn 'lower', do đó cần dùng 'than' để so sánh với số liệu quý trước.

part5.question: Seldom _______ such a rapid expansion in the retail sector been witnessed.
part5.explain: Đảo ngữ với từ phủ định/bán phủ định 'Seldom'. Động từ chính là 'been witnessed' (hiện tại hoàn thành), trợ động từ phải là 'has'.

part5.question: The contractor failed to meet the deadline, _______ a penalty fee.
part5.explain: Mệnh đề phân từ hiện tại (present participle) chỉ kết quả của mệnh đề trước đó. Dùng V-ing 'incurring' (gánh chịu).

part5.question: _______ to popular belief, the company is not planning to lay off any employees.
part5.explain: Cụm từ cố định 'Contrary to popular belief' (Trái với niềm tin/suy nghĩ phổ biến).

part5.question: The CEO's speech was not only inspiring _______ highly informative.
part5.explain: Cấu trúc tương quan 'not only ... but also ...' (không những ... mà còn ...).

part5.question: Should you _______ any further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact our support team.
part5.explain: Đảo ngữ câu điều kiện loại 1: Should + S + V_bare. Chọn 'require'.

part6.text:
To: All Employees
From: Management

blanks.explain: Sau động từ 'minimize' cần một danh từ làm tân ngữ. 'disruption' (sự gián đoạn) là danh từ hợp lý.
Đầu câu mệnh lệnh yêu cầu ai đó làm gì, dùng 'Please' (Vui lòng).
Chủ ngữ 'It' (văn phòng mới) số ít, diễn tả sự thật hiện tại, động từ 'feature' cần thêm 's' -> 'features' (có đặc điểm/cung cấp).
Sau tính từ sở hữu 'your' cần một danh từ. 'cooperation' (sự hợp tác) là đáp án đúng.

Subject: Your recent order #4992
Dear Ms. Henderson,

Thank you for shopping at TechGear Online. We are writing to update you on the status of your recent order. 

Unfortunately, the wireless headphones you __(1)__ are currently out of stock. We expect a new shipment to arrive early next week. We can either hold your entire order until the headphones are available, __(2)__ we can ship the rest of your items now and send the headphones later at no extra shipping cost.

__(3)__, please reply to this email to let us know your preference. If we do not hear from you within 48 hours, we will proceed with the second option by default.

Sincerely,
TechGear Customer Support

blanks.explain: Sự việc đặt hàng đã xảy ra trong quá khứ nên dùng thì quá khứ đơn 'ordered'.
Cấu trúc 'either ... or ...' (hoặc ... hoặc ...).
'Therefore' (Vì vậy, Do đó) dùng để đưa ra kết luận hoặc hệ quả, yêu cầu khách hàng phản hồi.
Sau 'this' cần danh từ số ít. 'delay' (sự chậm trễ) là hợp lý.

blanks.explain: Trước danh từ 'repairs' cần một tính từ. 'essential' (cần thiết, thiết yếu) là đáp án đúng.
Câu điều kiện loại 1: 'If you have any medical conditions..., please contact...'.
'ensure' (đảm bảo) thường được dùng với nghĩa đảm bảo điều gì đó sẽ xảy ra (đảm bảo độ tin cậy lâu dài).
Sau tính từ sở hữu 'your' cần danh từ. 'understanding' (sự thấu hiểu, thông cảm) là phù hợp nhất.

By Rosanne Villalobos
THISTLETON (6 February)—Larchmere Print and Packaging will move its operations to a larger site north of town, the firm confirmed this week. Its Wesley Street premises can no longer hold the presses needed to meet rising orders for folded cartons. The new building at Hollowbrook Industrial Park offers 4,200 square meters, nearly twice the present production area.
"We have been turning work away for want of room for a fourth press," said Ingrid Solberg, the operations manager. "How orders are taken and handled will not alter, and no counter post will be lost."
The handover will proceed in three stages. In the first, beginning on 2 March, contractors will fit out the new building. In the second, from 20 April, company engineers will move the presses across, and although production will pause briefly, no order deadline will be affected. In the third, beginning on 1 June, the order collection point will transfer to Hollowbrook.
Ordering by telephone or through the online portal remains unchanged, as do current prices and counter opening hours. The one difference for customers is that from the third stage, finished work must be collected at Hollowbrook rather than on Wesley Street. The firm also plans to hire 12 production staff. Applications close on 21 February and should be sent to its personnel office.

HARTWELL (12 September)— The Hartwell Growers' Market is opening a second trading location to keep up with rising demand. — [1] —. Over the past year, the Saturday market has welcomed an average of more than 4,000 shoppers each week, roughly double the number recorded two years earlier.
The market has operated on Meadow Street for eight years, where 25 stalls sell fresh produce, baked goods, and crafts every Saturday morning. Organizers say the growth is largely the result of several new farms joining from the surrounding valley, which has widened the range of goods on offer and drawn visitors from neighboring towns.
To ease the crowding, a second market will open at Cranford Square, close to the town's central bus stop. — [2] —. The new site will run on Wednesdays and Thursdays from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., with room for up to 40 stalls, and sellers will pay a rental fee of 20 dollars per day.
"The weekday market means that people who work on weekends can finally buy fresh vegetables and bread from local producers," said Beatrice Nolan, director of the Hartwell Community Market Association. — [3] —. Samuel Ortega, who sells honey and preserves at the Meadow Street site, added that the extra days would help him reach customers he had never met before.

Thornhedge Nursery Welcomes Visitors to Its Second Store
ARDENFORD (14 March) - Thornhedge Nursery, a family-run garden business known across the region for its wide selection of shrubs and flowering plants, has opened a second store on Wexley Lane in Ardenford.
The business began eleven years ago as a single stall selling potted herbs at a weekend market. Yvonne Castellan, who started Thornhedge and continues to oversee its day-to-day operations, said the company's steady growth had come from modest beginnings. "We had only a small table and a few dozen plants when we opened," she
recalled
. "Every step since then has been guided by what our customers ask us for, and this new store is the clearest sign yet of how far that has taken us."
The Ardenford store occupies a converted warehouse and features a bright indoor display hall, a covered courtyard for larger trees, and a separate room set aside for teaching. Wide aisles allow visitors to move easily between the seasonal arrangements, and a central advice counter is staffed throughout the day so that shoppers can ask about plant care before they buy.
The new location also introduces a program of hands-on planting workshops, something the first store was never able to accommodate. Sessions are held twice each week, and each one is limited to sixteen participants so that staff can give individual attention. Topics range from container gardening to the care of indoor foliage.
The store is open every day except Tuesday, from nine in the morning until six in the evening. General entry carries no charge, and throughout the opening month the nursery is offering each visitor a complimentary young seedling to take home.
"A garden center should be a place where people feel welcome to learn, not only to buy," Ms. Castellan said. "I hope this store gives our neighbours somewhere to spend an afternoon and to leave with something they have grown themselves."

Patrons are encouraged to reserve their seats without delay through the company's website at www.braytontheatre.org/season, where the complete performance schedule has been posted.

September 20 — For more than forty years, Foxglove Craft Supply has sold yarn, paint, clay, and countless other materials to the makers of Denbury. In all that time, however, the shop has never once offered guided classes of its own. That is about to change. Beginning next month, the store will run The Maker Sessions, a series of hands-on workshops in which shoppers can learn a new craft from start to finish and walk out with something they have made themselves.
Delia Faust, who manages events at the store, said the idea came from customers themselves. "People buy the supplies and then tell us they are not quite sure where to begin," she said. "We wanted to give them a place to sit down, try something, and leave with a finished piece they made by hand."
To introduce the program, Foxglove will hold a free taster afternoon on Saturday, October 5, when visitors can watch short demonstrations and ask questions at no cost. Made to Last: The Quiet Craft of Fairholme
By Adrian Colville
For more than thirty years, Fairholme has built a quiet reputation among people who care how a machine is made. Every model leaving its small workshop begins with a hand-brazed steel frame, a broad spread of gears for climbing and descending, and hand-laced wheels chosen for strength rather than weight.
Its founders remain sure that a frame built slowly will outlast several cheaper ones. Each joint is filed and polished before painting, and every finished frame is tested to be certain it can
handle
years of daily use on rough ground.
Fairholme makes no effort to court racers or weekend competitors. Its owners are the people who ride the same route to work each morning, carry shopping home each evening, and expect a machine ready to go in any weather.
One detail that longtime owners praise is the fully enclosed chain cover. By sealing the chain away from rain and grit, it saves riders from marking their clothes when they set out in ordinary dress rather than cycling gear. A built-in dynamo, meanwhile, powers the lamps, sparing riders the worry of flat batteries after dark.
Whatever the model, the goal stays the same: a machine that asks little and serves for many years.

Since opening its doors in Cedar Valley, Larkfield Dance Studio has built its name on youth instruction. By Damon Whitby | Cedar Valley Living | September 22
For years, Larkfield Dance Studio has been a familiar fixture for Cedar Valley's youngest dancers. This October, the Maple Row studio is trying something rather different: a beginners' course built entirely for adults, and one that its organizers hope will draw people who assumed their dancing days had passed them by.
The eight-week program, called First Steps on the Floor, begins Monday, October 6 and will be led by instructor Lorena Bassett. Aimed squarely at people who have never taken a dance class of any kind, the course walks students through the fundamentals of ballroom dancing at an unhurried pace. Organizers are also quick to note that no partner is required to sign up.
"So many adults tell me they have always wanted to try this, but they were afraid of being the only beginner in the room," said Bassett. "This class is for exactly those people. Nobody here is expected to know a single step on day one."
The term costs $95, and registration is available only through the studio's website at www.larkfielddance.com.

Introducing the Saturday Starters Program at Millhaven Swim School
We are pleased to announce a new weekend course for children who are learning to swim for the very first time. Beginning next month, the Saturday Starters Program will offer small-group lessons every Saturday morning for young swimmers between the ages of four and seven. The decision has not been taken lightly. For several terms our weekday beginner sessions have been running at full capacity, and each new intake has left a growing number of households hoping for a place we could not offer. Rather than continue to turn newcomers away, we have chosen to open a second slate of beginner places on Saturdays so that every child who wishes to begin can find one.
Millhaven has served local children for more than fifteen years. The school is led by head coach Rosalind Frayne, who competed at the national level before moving into teaching, and every instructor now on our pool deck was trained personally by Rosalind — including two colleagues she took on this spring — before taking charge of a class of her own.
Households already enrolled with us need do nothing at all. Weekday schedules are unchanged, existing bookings remain valid, and the online account through which you manage them will continue to work as before. The Saturday sessions are reserved strictly for children who are only now beginning to swim; current pupils should therefore stay with their weekday slot rather than transfer across. To reserve a place in the new program, please visit the enrollment page on our website or telephone the front desk at 555-0142. Places are limited and will be allocated in the order that requests are received.

Merrifield Observatory Opens Its Evenings to the Public
The Halbrook Public Observatory in Merrifield will launch a new after-dark viewing program, Starlight Evenings, beginning on 5 March. Running every week through the spring, the program invites residents to observe the night sky under the guidance of the observatory's staff rather than through a booked private tour.
Central to the program is a newly installed 400-millimeter reflecting telescope, the largest instrument the observatory has ever operated. It is the reason many residents will notice something new about the observatory this spring. Because it requires careful handling and darker conditions, the telescope is dedicated exclusively to the program's advanced deep-sky sessions. The introductory and family sessions will continue to use the observatory's smaller viewing scopes and its outdoor terrace.
"For years our finest equipment was available only to visiting researchers," said Dr. Rosa Meakin, the observatory's director. "This program is about opening those evenings to everyone in Merrifield who has ever wanted to look up and see more of what is there."
The launch comes at a time when
chances
for public astronomy in the region have grown scarce. The nearby Denholm Science Centre reduced its evening public hours last year following a review of its program spending, and the Ivelford Astronomy Club has since suspended its monthly open sessions, leaving few options for residents hoping to view the sky after dark.
Seats for each session are capped at 20 per evening, and the observatory encourages early booking. A full schedule of the spring sessions appears below.

Protecting the Art You Love: Small Steps That Make a Difference
MARWICK (14 March)—A favorite painting or a framed family photograph can lose its color, and much of its value, faster than most owners expect. Living Spaces Monthly spoke with framing specialist Nadia Sorensen about the simple habits that keep artwork looking its best for decades.
Her first piece of advice concerns location. Never hang a picture where direct sunlight falls on it, she warns, because steady light will fade the colors within a few years. She also recommends keeping artwork out of kitchens and bathrooms, where changing humidity can loosen the paper and encourage mold.
The choice of materials matters just as much. "The single most important decision is the board placed behind the piece," Ms. Sorensen said. "Ordinary cardboard contains acids that turn yellow and stain the artwork, sometimes within months. Only acid-free board will truly protect it." She adds that the glass should be dusted gently and that frames should be kept well away from heaters and radiators.
Readers who would rather leave the work to a professional can visit Halden Framing Studio, which serves the Marwick area from its single location on Pinewood Row. Ms. Sorensen frames every piece with acid-free board, just as she recommends to readers. The studio does not deliver or operate branches in other towns; all framing is completed on site. Studio members are also invited to a free framing workshop held once a month.

Wrenford Gardens Introduces Guided Heritage Walks
WEXBRIDGE (14 February)—Wrenford Botanical Gardens will begin offering a new guided tour, the Wrenford Heritage Garden Walk, on 3 March. Places can be booked from this week.
The gardens were first laid out by Edmund Castellan more than a hundred years ago, when the grounds formed part of a large private estate. For much of the last century the land was closed to the public, and only in recent decades has it become a garden that anyone may visit.
The gardens are now run by their director, Bernard Mott. Visitors can enjoy a carefully restored greenhouse, a plant shop, and the Fernbank Café, all set within the grounds.
Each walk will be led by Margaret Ainsley, the gardens' senior horticulturist, who has cared for the grounds for many years and knows the history of nearly every planting along the route.
Later in the year, the gardens hope to add a series of evening walks for visitors who prefer a quieter time of day.
To reserve a place, visit www.wrenfordgardens.co.uk.
----------------------
★★★★
Wrenford Heritage Garden Walk — reviewed by Gerald Voss
I took part in the very first Wrenford Heritage Garden Walk on 24 March, and it was a delightful morning that I would happily recommend. Our guide, Margaret Ainsley, was full of knowledge and clearly loves the place. She led us along a winding route past the oldest trees and told us how the grounds had changed over the years.
The walk finished with complimentary tea and slices of cake in the Fernbank Café, which was a lovely touch. We also stepped inside the beautifully restored greenhouse, and the plant shop near the exit had a wonderful selection of seedlings to take home.

To: Angela Ruiz
From: Nolan Pierce
Subject: Designer recommendation
Date: March 12
Dear Angela,
You asked last week whether I knew a reliable graphic designer for your product catalog, and I am glad to recommend Curtis Holloway.
Curtis spent several years at Brookmere Creative Agency before opening his own practice. When I asked why he had struck out on his own, he explained that what he valued most was sitting down directly with the local business owners he served, rather than routing every decision through account managers. That focus is clear in how he operates today. He works almost entirely with small companies in our region, and he takes on several kinds of projects, including logos, printed brochures, and graphics for websites.
If you decide to reach out, Curtis offers a first meeting at no cost, so you can describe your project and view samples of his earlier work before committing to anything. You do not need to book weeks in advance, and the meeting is open to anyone considering his services, not only first-time clients. Once a project begins, he usually delivers the finished files within two weeks.
I engaged Curtis myself last quarter for our conference materials, and I was impressed from start to finish. When the completed booklet reached my supervisor, Ms. Loretta Vance, she was delighted with the result and asked who had produced it. That reaction alone should tell you a great deal about the quality of his work.
Please feel free to mention my name when you contact him. I am confident you will find him easy to work with, and I would be happy to answer any further questions.
Best regards,
Nolan Pierce

Calderwood introduced its very first model in the year it opened, and that watch still sells steadily today. This month the company adds a new collection led by the Nocturne, its most recent design.
Calderwood designs and manufactures all of its wristwatches in-house, and the complete range is carried by retailers across the country.

Technical Support Portal — User Guide
For: All staff and contractors
Maintained by: Workplace Systems Team
The Workplace Systems Team has launched a single online intake channel for everyday technology needs, and every worker should use it before contacting us any other way. --[1]--.
Previously, colleagues reached us by telephone or messaged a team member directly, and cases often sat in one inbox or were forgotten between shifts. The portal was built to replace that scattered pattern: routine tickets are now logged, timestamped, and routed to the correct specialist automatically, without a person on our side deciding where they should go. --[2]--. Staff and contractors still see the same team behind the scenes, but the intake path has changed.
The portal at a glance
Access point: the Help link on the staff home page
Eligible users: all staff and contractors with a company login
Request types: system access, equipment, and account changes
Expected response: within two business days for standard cases
Escalation: call the Workplace Systems Team support line
To start, open the portal from the Help link and choose one of the categories listed above. Selecting the wrong category is the most common reason a case is delayed, so pause to match your issue to the closest label before you continue. --[3]--. Once the form is complete, submit it; the system returns a reference number on screen, and you can enter that number on the Status page at any time to see the latest update.
One situation should not be handled through the portal. If a single fault is stopping several people from working at the same time, telephone the support line right away instead of filing a ticket. --[4]--. Personal messages to individual team members are still discouraged for any request, urgent or not, because they bypass the record we rely on to track workload.
For questions, write to the Workplace Systems Team.

Subject: Scheduled Annual Safety Inspection of Your Apartment
Dear Resident,
This letter is to inform you that the management office has scheduled the annual safety inspection for all apartments in the West Wing. A member of our maintenance team will visit each unit during the week of 14 April. The inspection confirms that heating units and smoke alarms function correctly, and it produces the compliance certificate that the building's insurance carrier requires each year.
A single technician will be carrying the testing equipment from one unit to the next. To make this transport manageable, the visits have been arranged one floor at a time rather than by individual request. This lets the technician finish a whole floor in a single morning and keeps the disruption to each hallway short.
On the day of your visit, the technician will need to reach the water heater, the hallway smoke alarm, and the cabinet beneath the kitchen sink. Although the check takes only a few minutes, it cannot be completed from the doorway. --[1]--. Please make sure these three areas are clear before the technician arrives. If any of these points is blocked, the technician cannot complete the check and will have to return on a later date. --[2]--.
If the assigned day is not convenient, you may request one alternative appointment by writing to the office at least three days in advance. --[3]--.
We are grateful for your cooperation in helping us complete these visits smoothly. --[4]--.
Please note that this notice applies to West Wing residents only; East Wing inspections will be announced separately. The office may be reached by telephone during business hours for general questions, but any request to change an appointment must be submitted in writing.
Sincerely,
Douglas Fenner
Property Manager, Wexford Court Apartments

THE RIVERSIDE COMMUNITY BULLETIN
Local Business
Marden Trust Reorganizes Branch Services
By Dana Whitmore, Staff Reporter
Marden Trust Bank has changed the way customers are served at its Cranbrook Avenue Branch. Instead of lining up at a single counter for every request, visitors are now directed to separate zones according to the type of help they need. A notice about the arrangement was posted in the lobby on Monday morning.
Branch manager Colette Duarte said the change followed months of customer surveys showing that shared waiting lines were the main source of complaints. "People waiting to deposit a check were often held up behind those with longer requests," she said. "Separating our services means each visit moves more quickly."
Under the new arrangement, loan officers no longer share the main floor with tellers. Customers seeking a personal loan or a mortgage now sit down with an officer in a private room away from the counters. Everyday account tasks have also been grouped together: opening a new personal account and registering for online banking are now handled at one welcome point rather than at two different desks.
Ms. Duarte encouraged customers to check the printed directory near the entrance, or to ask a floor assistant, before deciding where to wait.

Entry lines grew long at busy hours, so we added self-service.

Book online for an access code. Hold it at the self-scan reader on arrival, and keep your boarding pass ready.

Home Delivery and Installation Service — Meadowbrook Appliance Center
Rating: 4 out of 5 stars
Posted by newkitchen_beth on March 14
Last month I finally replaced the dishwasher that came with my apartment, and I bought a new one from Meadowbrook Appliance Center. --[1]--. I am posting this because helpful reviews made my own decision much easier, and I want to do the same for other shoppers. The crew arrived right at the start of the promised window and began with my old machine, which had rusted along the base and leaked whenever it ran. --[2]--. They wrapped it in a blanket and carried it out without marking a single wall. The new unit is a Northvale Appliances model, and that company's factory is known for its quiet, low-energy designs. --[3]--. The two installers connected it, ran a test cycle, and explained every setting before they left. The entire setup took about forty minutes. My one small complaint is that they left the empty cardboard boxes for me to break down and throw out myself. --[4]--.
Overall, a smooth experience — recommended for anyone who would rather not install a heavy appliance alone.

Oakvale Food Cooperative — A Community-Owned Grocery
Welcome! This page is for anyone thinking about shopping with us as a member. Below you will find how our cooperative works and the simple steps to join.
How our co-op works
Oakvale is owned by the people who shop here. Since we opened in 2009, our members have shared in the decisions that shape the store, from the products we stock to the local farms we partner with. Members are not employees; they are neighbors who help guide the store and buy their weekly groceries here. Today more than 1,200 households hold a membership. Two years ago, members funded a new solar roof, which now supplies part of our electricity. All members also receive a monthly newsletter and reduced prices on cooking workshops.
A shared goal this year
This year we are working to open a fresh bakery counter at the back of the store. Building it is a demanding project that cannot be finished by staff alone. It will require both contributions from members and hours of volunteer help. We expect the counter to open before the end of the year, offering bread baked on site each morning.
Becoming a member
Joining is easy. First, complete a short form at the customer service desk. Second, pay a one-time equity share of $25, which is refunded if you ever decide to leave. Third, attend a brief orientation so you understand how the store runs. There is no monthly charge, and your share makes you a part-owner right away.
Store hours: Monday to Saturday, 8:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M. Questions? Speak with any staff member or stop by the service desk. We look forward to welcoming you.

Workshop Spotlight
Cut, Stitch, Repeat
By Rebecca Lyle
A quiet studio in Braxton is teaching newcomers to make their own leather goods entirely by hand.
On a side street in Braxton, behind the wide windows of Thornbury Leather Studio, a row of visitors bend over their workbenches, pressing needles through strips of tan hide. None of them had made anything from leather before this month, and that is exactly the point. This spring the studio began offering a set of hands-on workshops built for complete beginners, and the seats have been filling quickly.
The program is arranged in three levels. First Stitch, the entry point, is a single two-hour session that requires no experience and sends participants home with a finished card holder. Everyday Carry runs across two evenings and guides makers through cutting, dyeing, and assembling a folded wallet. The longest option, Satchel Studio, fills a full weekend and ends with a completed shoulder bag. Each level
draws
a different sort of visitor, from the curious first-timer to the hobbyist ready for a larger project. Tools and materials are provided at every level.
Every session is led in person by Julian Reyes, who opened the studio after spending three years apprenticing with a saddlemaker in Florence. "I was taught slowly, by hand, and that is how I teach here," Reyes said. "People are surprised by how much they can finish in one sitting once someone shows them where to place the needle."
Classes run on weekday evenings and weekends, and places can be reserved through the studio's website. Reyes recommends First Stitch as a starting point for anyone unsure whether the craft suits them.
----------------------
Rating: 5 out of 5 stars
Workshop attended: First Stitch
Would recommend: Yes
Review title: Made something real in one afternoon
Posted by: newtocraft_gina
Date: May 14
I booked the shortest class on the list because I only wanted to find out whether making things by hand was for me, and I had never picked up a leather tool in my life. Two hours later I walked out with a card holder that I had cut and stitched myself. The person leading the session was endlessly patient. At one point he mentioned that he had been shaping and repairing leather since he was a boy, and it showed in the way he fixed our mistakes without ever taking the work out of our hands. The studio sits inside an old glove factory just a few streets from my apartment, one I had walked past for years without going in. I am already looking at signing up for the wallet class next.

The retailer, which has run its established stores in Redmill for more than a decade, picked Westport for its latest expansion and is said to be weighing a further store in Northgate.

Chess Championship to Return This Autumn
Regional association invites players of every level to compete in Riverton
By Colin Ashby, Community Affairs Correspondent
RIVERTON — September 18
The Selby District Chess Association will hold its annual Selby Open Championship at Riverton Civic Hall this autumn, and organizers say they expect one of the strongest turnouts in years. The event is open to players of every skill level, from schoolchildren trying competitive play for the first time to seasoned club members.
For more than a decade the association has
served
the wider county, and alongside the championship it also runs regular monthly tournaments in the neighboring towns of Hadleigh and Penhurst. "We want this championship to reach every corner of the region, not simply one town," said Malcolm Frost, the association's president. He added that membership has climbed steadily each year and that newcomers are always welcome.
Entries close on October 6, and the championship itself is scheduled for Saturday, October 14. The entry fee is fifteen dollars, which covers all rounds and a light lunch. Interested players may sign up in person at the association's office on weekday afternoons or by telephone during the same hours.

The Selby Open Championship was held at Riverton Civic Hall on Saturday, December 6. The contest drew more than 120 players, the largest field it has ever recorded, and spectators filled the hall throughout the day. Organizers reported that every scheduled round finished on time despite the crowded program.
In the Open division, Carol Sutton captured first place after a tense final round that lasted well past the afternoon. The junior title went to Simon Hale, a newcomer competing in only his second tournament. Chief judge Raymond Delaney praised the overall standard of play, while association president Malcolm Frost thanked the many volunteers who kept the long day running smoothly.
Full standings for every division will be posted at the association's office and on its website by December 20, where players may also find details of next year's calendar.

Community Spotlight
By Frances Doyle
The Larkmead Community Craft Center is looking for a few extra pairs of hands, and it hopes local hobbyists will answer the call.
A Familiar Face
Leading the effort is Estelle Monroe, who spent more than fifteen years teaching art at a nearby secondary school before retiring three years ago. Since then she has volunteered at the center every week, and this autumn she takes charge of its expanding beginner workshop program. The classes
draw
dozens of residents each month, from schoolchildren to retirees, and Monroe says the waiting list keeps growing.
Lending a Hand
To keep pace, the center needs volunteer assistants who can support newcomers during sessions. Assistants set out materials, answer simple questions, and encourage first-timers who feel unsure. The program is meant to welcome enthusiastic hobbyists rather than trained professionals, and Monroe stresses that a friendly, patient manner matters far more than any formal qualifications. There is one practical condition: because assistants work alongside beginners at the worktable, the center asks that each volunteer already practice at least one craft of their own. Anyone interested can complete a short interest form, available at the front desk or on the center's website.
Have a hobby you love to share? Larkmead wants to hear from you.

Community News
By Gordon Pyle
The Bramford Historical Society will open its new Local History Center to the public next Saturday, offering residents a permanent home for the town's records, photographs, and everyday objects. The center occupies the former Trescott Flour Mill on Bell Lane, a stone building that stood empty for nearly twenty years before volunteers restored it over two summers. The ground floor holds a reading room and a small exhibit gallery, and the upper floor has been fitted out for workshops and document storage.
"A history center is only as rich as the community that fills it," said Ronald Ashworth, the society's director. "I would encourage every household in Bramford to look through their attics and drawers and donate old letters, maps, and family photographs, so that the collection reflects the whole town."
Residents who wish to take part may bring items to the center throughout opening week or ask a volunteer about lending materials for copying. To learn more, call the society office at 555-0148.

3. The session on caring for old documents may only be led by a volunteer who currently holds an archival preservation certificate, as fragile items will be handled directly.
I spent several summers helping to clear the old Trescott Flour Mill before its restoration began, so I know the upper floor well. If you are unsure where anything is kept, please ask me.
Cynthia Barlow

★★★★☆ | Custom Color Matching
Tamara Vogt | Foxwood | September
I brought in a fabric swatch from my living room curtains and asked the counter to match it as a flat wall paint. The staff member who helped me was careful and thorough. He tested several formulas before settling on the right one, and I could tell this is a store that has been doing custom work for quite some time. Business Briefs
The Bexley District Business Council has opened applications for its annual Community Improvement Grants. The program provides funding to local organizations for neighborhood projects within the district.
The grants are financed through a portion of annual membership fees paid by the Council's 150 member businesses. Eligible applicants must be registered nonprofit groups and must demonstrate that at least 30 percent of total project value will come from volunteer labor or donated materials. Awards fall into three categories: Public Space Enhancement (up to $4,000), Youth and Education Programs (up to $3,500), and Community Safety Improvements (up to $5,000).
"The strongest proposals bring residents together around a shared goal," said Philip Renwick, chair of the grants committee.
Applications are available at bexleycouncil.example and must be submitted by March 15. Decisions will be announced by April 30.

To: All installation crews
From: Helen Mortimer, Fitting Supervisor
Date: February 27
Subject: Completion images and billing
From Monday, March 6, closing out a job will include one new step: photographing the finished work at the customer's home and sending the images to the office.
Why this is changing.
Over the past four months several accounts have gone unpaid for weeks because customers questioned marks and missing pieces that we could not account for once the crew had left. Some of you have called this extra paperwork at the end of a long day, and I understand that, but we have nothing to show what we handed over. Every van already carries a tablet, so no new equipment is needed.
Each set must show the following:
[1] the whole run of units with every door and drawer closed
[2] the joint where the counter meets the wall
[3] the toe boards along the floor
[4] the inside of one upper unit with its shelves in place
[5] the floor and walls beside the finished units
On jobs of more than twelve units, add a wide view from the opposite corner. A sample set has already been circulated to crew leaders.
The images must be uploaded before the van comes back in. The office cannot release the bill for a job until the record is on file, so a set that arrives the next morning holds up payment. Staff here will match each set to the invoice.
Who is covered now.
For the next four weeks the step applies only to the three crews at the north yard, where Culver Timber Supply will keep delivering materials to each address as before. Crew leaders in that group will check every set before it is sent. When the four weeks are up, the remaining crews will hear from me about a short training session. If customers continue to raise questions after that, we may ask for a signature on site as well.
This notice is posted in the tool room. Each crew leader must add initials beside the crew number.

Larchmont Property Care — Winter Clearing Register
Registered properties are cleared overnight without a single telephone call.
How enrollment works
1. Send us the enrollment form with the address of every entrance and parking area you want covered.
2. A supervisor walks the property with your staff, marks the lines our machines will follow, and places the equipment listed below.

Left on site

Waves that ran as allocated
1. The reception level and mail room group left the floor inside its slot, and the name list handed in was complete and correct.

PROGRAM NEWS
Category Panels Take Over the Awards Judging
By Bernard Tomlin, Members' Bulletin
What has changed.
For several years, every entry to the Alliance Awards was read by the same in-house committee at the association office. That committee now prepares the scoring guide only. Each award category is reviewed instead by a small group of people who put their names forward from member businesses. "A single committee could not read every entry with the care it deserved," said Yvette Bouchard, awards coordinator. "People who run a business judge these entries better than we did."
How a sitting runs.
Every sitting opens with the chair going through the scoring guide with the panel, before any entry is opened. Entries are then scored one at a time, and each panel agrees on its shortlist before leaving the room.
Before you attend.
The placements now posted are provisional. Checking of entries continues to the end of February, and a panel may still be altered where a category gains or loses entries. Volunteers are asked to confirm their attendance with the awards office by February 20.

----------------------
Late Shopping Evenings Draw Steady Crowds
By Janet Whelan, Local Business
Shops in central Havelock stayed open until 9:00 p.m. on two evenings last week, and the Havelock Retailers' Association reports steady visitor numbers.
"Thursday was busier than any Saturday this year, and most of those who came in had never visited us," said Arnold Deming, who keeps a bookshop on Priory Lane.
The blocks did not trade on the evenings first published. The South Block shops opened late on Wednesday, October 8, and the North Block on Thursday, October 9, the members having agreed to exchange the two dates. Every participating shop appeared in a leaflet delivered across the town.
The association, which meets on the last Tuesday of each month, has forty-one members, and thirty-four opened on one of the two evenings. Printing and delivery were divided among them by frontage. Officers say a further promotion is planned, but no date is fixed.

Combining Rewards Balances: Program Rules
For member businesses holding accounts at more than one branch.
A. Who may ask, and how
Both accounts must be registered to the same member business, and the request must be put in writing by the person named as the contact on each account. Requests from other staff are returned without action.
B. Credit that carries across
Credit earned on supply orders carries across in full. Credit awarded through a bonus offer carries across at half its value, and the reduction is applied before the two totals are added.
C. What a combined balance cannot buy
A combined balance may not be used for any category supplied by an outside company rather than from the program's own stock. Those items must be claimed against a single account.
D. Timing
Requests are settled within ten business days. Credit that expires during that period cannot be restored.
Questions may be sent to the Rewards Administration Desk.

Overdue equipment accepted at the counter, with borrowing rights restored

Nothing I read before booking told me where the limits of this arrangement lie, so I am setting them out here.
Our lease ended nine weeks before the new floor was ready, and buying desks we would then store would have cost more than hiring. We took 24 pieces. Delivery staff removed the protective covers on arrival.
The desks and seating were sound. The three storage cabinets, though, were too shallow to hold our files upright. An exchange must be requested while at least fourteen days of the term remain, and we were inside that window, so I asked for deeper units. They arrived four days later rather than the next working day. I claimed nothing off the invoice and booked a second short hire in February.
The total came to $2,150, which our relocation budget
covered
easily, though delivery and collection are billed separately and the rate list does not say so.

Does not suit: teams with unusual storage needs, or terms under three weeks.

Changes Ahead at Renshaw Stationers
Local Business Section — By Ian Furlong
Millbrook, May 2
Frances Duvall, who opened Renshaw Stationers and has directed it ever since, will step back from daily management at the end of this month. Two members of her staff, Grace Abbott and Emil Kovacs, will take on the business jointly from June 1.
The store began in 1981 as a counter at the back of a printing works and has traded from its present address on the town's main business street for more than forty years. It supplies notebooks, filing materials, and desk equipment to local offices and to schools across the district.
Ms. Abbott began as a delivery driver and now keeps the accounts, while Mr. Kovacs has taken orders at the front counter for eighteen years. Staffing will remain as it is. "The name above the door will not change, and neither will the way we trade," Mr. Kovacs said.
The store will close on May 18 while new shelving is installed inside, and it will reopen at the same address on May 26. Orders may be placed by e-mail throughout the closure, with no charge added for delivery. Deliveries themselves begin again on the reopening day, and a customer who needs an order before then may collect it from the company's storage unit on Kestrel Lane.
Ms. Duvall will keep an office upstairs two mornings a week until December. "I would rather leave the store to people who helped build it than to a stranger," she said. "Our nine employees are all staying, and the work goes on as before."

Midvale Business Review — Regional Business
Two Delivery Firms Now Operating as One
By Emmett Frawley, Winslow
The combination of Alderton Delivery Services and Halstead Transport is complete, and one operation now handles the scheduled deliveries and collections that the two companies previously carried out separately for business customers across the region.
For more than fifteen years, both companies had sent vans into many of the same districts on separate schedules. Neighboring streets were often called at on different mornings, and customers in outlying areas waited noticeably longer than those close to either depot. Halstead Transport had also run Saturday collections, which Alderton Delivery Services never offered.
Districts now served by one operation: 9
Employees kept on: 34
Shared name in use from: March
Customers do not need to take any action. Signed agreements, most of which run for twelve months, continue on their current terms until those terms end. No new paperwork is required, and charges will be reviewed only when an agreement comes up for renewal.
"Every driver and office employee has been kept on, and the shared name will appear on vans and paperwork in stages over several weeks rather than all at once," said Louise Brennan, the managing director. Timings for a few of the longer rounds will be examined again later in the year, and any changes will be announced well in advance.

BEXFORD, February 18 — Ravenscroft Linen Services announced today that a reduced-rate collection service will be available to its business customers from March 2. --[1]--.

Around the City
Performers to appear in Woodgate Square
Four pitches have been set aside for licensed acts.
By Miriam Whitaker, March 12
Why the program began.
Counts taken last summer showed that the number of people in Woodgate Square fell by nearly half after the lunch hour.
How places are assigned.
Acts are grouped by category, and only one act from each category performs in a block. Organizers say the shows should
draw
shoppers into the smaller streets behind the square.
"Store owners nearby reported slow afternoon trade," said Miguel Ocampo of the Woodgate Square Management Office. "The program is approved for one season only. If audiences grow, we will propose a second year."

----------------------
Local Shops and Services
Topic: broken frame, repair needed before a trip
Posted by Yvonne Pratt, 9:12 P.M., June 24
I have bought my glasses from Copeland Eyewear for years, always at the store nearest my apartment. It is the only one I can use, because I finish work at 6:30 P.M. and can never reach a counter earlier. The hinge on my frames snapped on Sunday.
I took them in this evening. The assistant explained that no repair work is done at that store. She said that items needing workshop attention are collected once a week, on Thursday, so mine would wait until then. I leave on July 12 and do not want to travel with taped frames. Has anyone found a quicker route?
Y. P.
----------------------
Handling of Repairs Sent Off the Premises
For customers, effective from June 1.
An item left for workshop attention is entered on a record card at the counter and held in the store until the weekly transfer round. The case and the original receipt are not needed.
Stores without a workshop of their own send work out on one fixed day each week. Finished work returns to the store where the item was left, normally about three weeks later, and it cannot be collected at the workshop.
No repair begins until the estimated charge has been approved. The workshop calls the number on the record card and waits for a reply. Payment is due on collection, not at hand-in.
A customer who needs an item sooner than that may ask, before that store's transfer day, for it to be sent to the Lowden Street store by next-day courier. An extra charge applies.
Customer Care Office, Copeland Eyewear
A copy of this notice is displayed beside every counter.
